title: Cristiano Ronaldo travels from Saudi Arabia to Spain for hamstring treatment, Jorge Jesus says
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has left Saudi Arabia and travelled to Spain to undergo treatment on a hamstring injury, Al Nassr head coach Jorge Jesus has said.

Jesus said Ronaldo’s injury required treatment in Madrid and would rule him out of Saturday’s Saudi Pro League fixture against Neom and their following game against Al-Khaleej Club on March 14.

It would be the first fixture that Ronaldo has missed through injury this season.

Al Nassr released a statement on Tuesday explaining the 41-year-old had sustained a hamstring injury against Al Fayha last Saturday. Al Nassr had been due to play Al Wasl of the United Arab Emirates in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two in midweek, but this was postponed due to the conflict in the Middle East.

“Ronaldo suffered a muscle injury in the last match, and after examination, it became clear that it needed rest and treatment, so we decided to send him to Spain, as we did with Ayman Yahya, (Inigo) Martinez and Sami Al-Najei this season,” Jesus told a press conference. “They all went to Spain for examinations and treatment.

“The medical team assessed Ronaldo’s condition and confirmed that he wouldn’t be able to participate in tomorrow’s match or the following one, so we allowed him to leave for Spain to receive treatment.”

Al Nassr had been set to play Al Wasl in the return leg of their AFC Champions League Two quarter-final tie this coming Wednesday, but this has also been postponed, with all of the competition’s fixtures in the region off following the U.S. and Israeli military attack on Iran and the subsequent retaliation.

The Athletic reported on Wednesday the SPL had written to its clubs to inform them that fixtures would go ahead as planned despite the escalating conflict.

Ronaldo is Al Nassr’s top scorer this season with 21 goals in 26 appearances across all competitions. He returned to the side in the middle of February, having missed two league matches due to a dispute over the running of the club, having felt let down by Al Nassr’s lack of January transfer activity.

“I do not know what our opponents’ strategy will be tomorrow without Ronaldo,” Jesus added. “But I think it could make a difference for them individually, although it is difficult for us to be affected collectively.

“The important thing is that the player who replaces Ronaldo tomorrow plays at a high tempo and with high effectiveness and tries to help us score as Ronaldo does.”

Al Nassr are top of the SPL, two points clear of second place Al Ahli.
